text:
alex: Heads-up — saw ~12% p99 latency increase on host-side after yesterday's runtime canary. Flamegraphs point to tokenization + ingress parse hot paths. Suspect kernel selection and batching hints changed.

meera: Where's the trace? stack?

alex: P99 spike manifests on long-conversation tails. perf capture: `perf top` shows `tokenizer::split_bytes` and `ingress::parse_frame`.

jamie: Dropped a flamegraph: https://internal/fg/606162.png

meera: Can you paste the perf collapsed lines? Also which model variant + quantization?

alex: model=v1.3-q4_0; dedicated pool; kernel selection log shows chosen kernel=`matmul_opt_v2` for sequences >512 — that changed in release 2026-03-18.

taylor: Interesting. We added a heuristic to prefer v2 when batch size < 4 to reduce memory. Could interact badly with streaming small-chunk tails.

alex: Exactly. Also KV cache pressure spikes coincide with ingress parse CPU upshift. When KV miss rate increases, we see more host-side preproc work.

jamie: Reproduced locally with a mini-bench. Steps:
```:
./bench --model v1.3-q4_0 --seq 1024 --clients 8 --streaming
perf record -g -o /tmp/perf.data ./bench ...
```
flame shows heavy call from `http2_writev` and `tokenize_shim::process_chunk`.

meera: Could be streaming chunk coalescing regression — we changed chunk-window heuristics recently.

rick (ops-bot): Deployed canary 2026-03-18 03:12 UTC -> 2026-03-18 10:45 UTC on pool-34

taylor: Quick experiment: revert kernel preference and bump autobatch threshold to 8. Anyone can try on canary1?

jamie: I ran a quick canary patch: reverted kernel choice and set batching_hint=8 — p99 dropped back to baseline in my microbench (12.3ms -> 10.9ms).

meera: Logs from proxy show repeated small GRPC writes: `writev(3) size=128 128 64` which increases syscall overhead. Suggest increasing coalesce window or aggregating small token frames.

alex: Agreed. Also noticed `tokenize_shim` copies bytes into temporary buffer per frame; that's extra memcopy. Patch in my branch avoids copy when frame aligned.

taylor: Put up PR: DONT_COPY_ON_ALIGN, and updated kernel selector test. Link: https://phabricator/pr/1234

jamie: Ran end-to-end with PR + batching_hint=8. Results: p50 unchanged; p95 -1%; p99 -9%. KV miss rates dropped by 3%.

meera: Important to validate under tail-heavy workloads. Can we add a microtest simulating many small streaming frames to CI stress?

alex: Added a `stream_small_frames` workload to perf-suite. Jenkins job: jenkins/perf/stream_small_frames -> scheduled.

rick (ci-bot): perf job queued: #8123

taylor: Next steps:
- merge kernel heuristic revert (short-term)
- apply DONT_COPY_ON_ALIGN (low-risk)
- tune coalesce window for grpc writev
- add CI stress for small streaming frames

meera: Also add telemetry for `writev` size distribution and kvcache miss correlation.

alex: I'll assemble a postmortem note and timeline. Thanks all :rocket: 

jamie: FYI I saw no change in GPU utilization; this is host CPU and syscall overhead.

meera: Great catch, alex. Ping me when PRs are ready for review.
